items.title: Batch job got 1205 "Lock wait timeout exceeded" error
items.body:
<!-- DO NOT THROW THIS AWAY -->
<!-- Fill out the FULL versions with patch versions -->

- Laravel Version: 8.78.1
- PHP Version: 8.0.13
- Database Driver & Version: Mysql  Ver 8.0.27
- Queue Driver: SQS

### Description:
I have some jobs always get 1205 "Lock wait timeout exceeded" errors at the first beginning of starting dispatching a batch.
After some digging, I think the assumption below may explain the error I got. Please correct me if you got other ideas about that.

When a batch has many jobs like over 10,000 jobs and each job can be finished in several seconds, the batch may take several minutes to dispatch all jobs to SQS, during that time some of the dispatched jobs that have been consumed by workers will be waiting MySQL lock to decrement the pending jobs number in `queued_job_batches` table that the MySQL lock is still being occupied by the dispatching process. After waiting for 50 seconds which is the MySQL `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` value but the dispatching still has not finished yet, an "SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1205 Lock wait timeout exceeded" error will be thrown in the worker process.

When dispatching, the below step may take a long time to finish and the MySQL transaction will lock the batch row for a long time.
https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/master/src/Illuminate/Bus/Batch.php#L186-L194
```php
        $this->repository->transaction(function () use ($jobs, $count) {
            $this->repository->incrementTotalJobs($this->id, $count);

            $this->queue->connection($this->options['connection'] ?? null)->bulk(
                $jobs->all(),
                $data = '',
                $this->options['queue'] ?? null
            );
        });
```

Some of the dispatched jobs that have been consumed by workers are trying to decrement pending jobs but will have to wait for the transaction above to commit.
https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/master/src/Illuminate/Bus/DatabaseBatchRepository.php#L138-L152
```php
    public function decrementPendingJobs(string $batchId, string $jobId)
    {
        $values = $this->updateAtomicValues($batchId, function ($batch) use ($jobId) {
            return [
                'pending_jobs' => $batch->pending_jobs - 1,
                'failed_jobs' => $batch->failed_jobs,
                'failed_job_ids' => json_encode(array_values(array_diff(json_decode($batch->failed_job_ids, true), [$jobId]))),
            ];
        });

        return new UpdatedBatchJobCounts(
            $values['pending_jobs'],
            $values['failed_jobs']
        );
    }
```

### Steps To Reproduce:

<!-- If possible, please provide a GitHub repository to demonstrate your issue -->
<!-- laravel new bug-report --github="--public" -->
I have a crontab that will dispatch a batch with over 9,000 jobs to SQS each day and most of the jobs just need several seconds to finish.
Every day I can observe some first jobs will throw errors "SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1205 Lock wait timeout exceeded" and a few minutes later the errors totally disappear.

Below is part of the exception trace:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9317172/150718931-69da3c97-f1eb-4c22-804c-897fbaedc196.png)

items.title: Handling deadlock caused by locking reads
items.body:
<!-- DO NOT THROW THIS AWAY -->
<!-- Fill out the FULL versions with patch versions -->

- Laravel Version: 5.8.38
- PHP Version: 7.4.9
- Database Driver & Version: MySQL 5.7.26

### Description:
Deadlock exception caused by locking reads (sharedLock or lockForUpdate) should be thrown and not just ignored and return empty results.


### Steps To Reproduce:
- Open two terminals for php artisan tinker
- Start transaction in the terminals (`DB::transaction()`)
- In T1, update a specific User
- In T2, update a specific User
- In T1, try to select number of Users with sharedLock()
- In T2, try to select number of Users with sharedLock()

Expected:
- Error / Exception thrown

Actual:
- Empty results returned

items.title: Database lock wait timeout after errors within transaction
causedByDeadlock() assumes MySQL returns errors in English.
items.body:
### Description:

I was checking out the automatic deadlock detection code and I noticed that instead of checking for an error number or exception type, it checks if the string contains text?

[FYI MySQL errors are not always in English](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.5/en/error-message-language.html).

If the underlying DB is PDO then I would propose checking for something like:

```
     $e instanceof PDOException &&
     $pdo->getAttribute(PDO::ATTR_DRIVER_NAME) == 'mysql' &&
     $e->errorInfo[0] == 40001 &&
     $e->errorInfo[1] == 1213
```

PS: Awesome feature!


### Steps To Reproduce:

Current code in master branch:

https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/master/src/Illuminate/Database/DetectsDeadlocks.php

    protected function causedByDeadlock(Exception $e)
    {
        $message = $e->getMessage();
        return Str::contains($message, [
            'Deadlock found when trying to get lock',
            'deadlock detected',
            'The database file is locked',
            'database is locked',
            'database table is locked',
            'A table in the database is locked',
            'has been chosen as the deadlock victim',
            'Lock wait timeout exceeded; try restarting transaction',
        ]);
    }

items.title: [5.5] database queue - transactions management fix
items.body:
- Database transactions management fix, rollback on exception.
- fixes #7046. With this patch job workers are able to recover from transaction deadlocks (instead of freezing)

EDIT, TLDR:
The bug: `rollback()` is not called for an opened transaction on `$this->database` object in `DatabaseQueue` if an Exception is thrown from any reason (e.g., deadlock, timeout). This leaves database object in inconsistent state (no `commit()` nor `rollback()` for started transaction). This is problem for DB workers / daemons.

5.5 solution: fixing transaction management by wrapping tsx in try/catch and adding `rollback()` to catch block. No breaking changes.

5.6 solution (potential): if 5.5 gets merged, refactor `DatabaseQueue` a bit so transactions are wrapped in closures - cleaner and safer. Removing nonintuitive `commit()` in `marshallJob()` (possibly breaking change).

items.title: 'SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1205 Lock wait timeout exceeded' error when test using DatabaseTransaction alongside Mockery Expection Declaration
items.body:
I have problem when writing test using mockery **[Expection Declaration](http://docs.mockery.io/en/latest/reference/expectations.html)** alongside `DatabaseTransaction` Trait. If first test failed because of `\Mockery\CountValidator\Exception` then other tests will have `SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1205 Lock wait timeout exceeded` error.

I think it's better to put `Mockery::close()` after `beforeApplicationDestroyCallbacks`. Because Mockery will check when `Mockery::close()`. I have try to move this and it works well.

```
    /**
     * Clean up the testing environment before the next test.
     *
     * @return void
     */
    public function tearDown()
    {
        if ($this->app) {
            foreach ($this->beforeApplicationDestroyedCallbacks as $callback) {
                call_user_func($callback);
            }

            $this->app->flush();

            $this->app = null;
        }

        if (property_exists($this, 'serverVariables')) {
            $this->serverVariables = [];
        }

        if (class_exists('Mockery')) {
            Mockery::close();
        }
    }
```

i'm Using Laravel 5.1. Here are my test
